source_text: Klagel. Jerem. 2, 16. «Ὁ« γὰρ ἐχθρὸς «ἡμῶν διάβολος περιέρχεται ὡς λέων ὠρυόμενος ζητῶν τίνα καταπίῃ« καὶ ὡς ὅφις ἐφ' ὴμᾶς ἀφιεὶς τὰ συρίγματα. πλὴν μὴ γένοιτο λέγειν αὐτὸν ὡς κατέπιον , μήτε καταλαβεῖν ἐν ἡμῖν ἡμέραν ἥν ὁ συγκαίων ἥλιος ἀπεργάζεται· εἴρηται γάρ· «ἡμέρας ὁ ἤλιος οὐ συγκαύσει σε( ἡδοναῖς γὰρ καὶ θυμῷ συγκαίει καὶ τὴν πλάνην ὡς ὡς φῶς καὶ γνῶσιν παρέχεται. ψάλλοντες οὐν ἐροῦμεν· «εἰ μὴ ὅτι κύριος ἦν ἐν ἡμῖν, , ἄρα ζῶντας ἂν κατέπιον ἡμᾶς‘, καὶ τὸ «λαμπτὴρ δὲ ἀσεβῶν σβεσθήσεται.
pass_a_gloss: For “our enemy the devil goes about as a roaring lion seeking whom he may steichos / wallow” and as a serpent sending the hissings upon us. Yet may it not come about that he say “I have steichos / wallowed,” nor that he overtake in us a day which the scorching sun works; for it has been said: “the sun will not scorch you by day”—for with pleasures and wrath he scorches and provides the error as light and knowledge. Singing psalms, then, we will say: “if the Lord had not been in us, then living they would have steichos / wallowed us,” and “the lamp of the impious will be quenched.”
pass_b_english: For “our enemy the devil goes about as a roaring lion seeking whom he may swallow” (Lamentations 2:16) and as a serpent sending the hissings upon us. Yet may it not come about that he say “I have swallowed,” (Psalm 124:2–3) nor that he overtake in us a day which the scorching sun works; for it has been said: “the sun will not scorch you by day” (Job 18:5)—for with pleasures and wrath he scorches and provides the error as light and knowledge. Singing psalms, then, we will say: “if the Lord had not been in us, then living they would have swallowed us,” (1 Peter 5:8) and “the lamp of the impious will be quenched.” (Psalm 121:6)
